audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagreed between layers — full read Yone/Yone/Skill/Skill/Yone/Skill/Yone against content Akali/Akali/Yone/Yone/Akali/Yone/Akali. On top of that the content layer contradicted itself: win[1] says Akali while whys[1] said the knockup was 'giving him the trade'.
audit.why: content win[] matches packet.levelChart exactly. Mortal Steel only becomes a knockup at two stacks, so levels 1-2 are not his; 3-5 are, once the knockup dash is reliable; level 6 is Akali's execute; first item is his crit spike; late is Akali's.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides flipped as one atomic group, and whys[1] rewritten so the content layer stops arguing with its own chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] attributed the first-item row to 'Yone's own ultimate coming online here'.
audit.why: Fate Sealed unlocks at level 6, one row earlier — the first-item row is his crit item, which spikes[2] already correctly names. The two entries disagreed about what causes the same swing.
audit.corrected: whys[5] now attributes the row to his crit item and the shield it feeds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound (E) was described as a dash — 'Q3 into E dash follow-ups', 'weave E dashes through minions', 'dual-form dash'. Fate Sealed (R) was described as an 'AoE knockup ultimate'. Spirit Cleave's shield was not mentioned anywhere.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is not a dash: Yone's spirit leaves his body with bonus move speed and is FORCED BACK to the body when it ends, repeating part of the damage. His dash is Mortal Steel at two stacks. Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and PULLS enemies toward him — no knockup, which changes whether knockup-dependent follow-up exists. And Spirit Cleave grants a shield on a 14-second clock that scales with champions hit, which is exactly what eats Akali's burst opener.
audit.corrected: Every E-dash reference replaced with Mortal Steel; Fate Sealed described as a blink-and-pull; the Spirit Cleave shield now stated in breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, phases[3].why and enemyWin.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns said 'count it out loud' without giving any number.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10s and Spirit Cleave is a flat 14s — those two numbers set every commit window in the lane.
audit.corrected: Both written in, along with the snap-back punish on the body he leaves behind.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin and breakdown.carry were structural templates.
audit.why: 'wins by landing X, denying your pattern' and 'Carry through deletions' paste onto any enemy.
audit.corrected: Regrounded on the shield, the knockup and the pull.

edits.before: Shroud online: the trade pattern is Q-auto, shroud the answer, Q again from the smoke. Most mids lose this exchange.
edits.after: Mortal Steel reaches two stacks and the empowered cast dashes him in with a knockup — that window is his, not yours.

edits.before: Passive-weave every trade: spell, walk out of the ring, auto the edge — the energy refunds pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s and eats your opener — force it out with a throwaway Q before you commit.

edits.before: First item spike: shroud trades become kill threats. Force the wave contact and punish every spell he whiffs.
edits.after: His crit item lands before yours, and it feeds the Spirit Cleave shield too — his all-in beats your shroud here.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Twilight Shroud has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1, 10s maxed — the spirit is dragged back to the body it left, so stand on the body and punish the snap. - Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s: bait it before you commit. - Fate Sealed is 120s and pulls, it never knocks up.

edits.before: Yone wins by landing Soul Unbound, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Yone wins by shielding through your opener with Spirit Cleave, landing the Mortal Steel knockup, and dragging you back with Fate Sealed.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Yone is the deletion — pop the Spirit Cleave shield with a throwaway Q, then R in and execute before 14s returns it.

edits.before: Yone's Q3 (third Mortal Steel cast) delivers a guaranteed knockup that outvalues your own combo at this level, giving him the trade.
edits.after: Your level 2 combo still beats his, because Mortal Steel needs two stacks before it dashes and knocks up, and he cannot bank them on you yet.

edits.before: Yone's own ultimate comes online here and gives him a temporary engage/teamfight edge that swings this phase back to him.
edits.after: His first crit item lands before yours, and it feeds both his all-in damage and the Spirit Cleave shield, swinging this phase to him.

edits.before: Yone hits 3 and starts landing Q3 (Mortal Steel knockup) into E dash follow-ups; if he catches your Q poke animation he can flip the trade hard before you have Shroud up on cooldown-free rotation.
edits.after: Yone hits 3 and starts landing the empowered Mortal Steel, which dashes him in and knocks up; if he catches your Q animation he flips the trade hard before Shroud is back off its 20-second cooldown.

edits.before: Yone's teamfight ultimate (knock-up AoE, dual-form dash) makes him a walking pick threat in 2+ item skirmishes, but you out-duel him 1v1 with Shroud vision denial and Twilight resets if he ever gets caught alone.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks him behind the last champion in the line and pulls everyone it hits toward him — a pick tool, not a knockup — but you still out-duel him 1v1 with Shroud vision denial if he is caught alone.

edits.before: With items you're back in control: Twilight Shroud lets you vanish from his skillshots and reset fights via Assassin's Mark stacks, and your reset-burst kit punishes any Yone caught even slightly out of position. Group fights still favor his AoE knockup ultimate if his team can follow up, so pick your all-ins around vision and cooldowns rather than diving into a stacked knockup.
edits.after: With items you're back in control: Twilight Shroud lets you vanish from his skillshots, and your reset-burst kit punishes any Yone caught even slightly out of position. Group fights still favour Fate Sealed, which blinks him past your line and drags everyone it hits back toward his team, so pick your all-ins around vision and his 120-second ultimate rather than walking into the pull.

edits.before: Weave E dashes through minions to reposition and threaten flank angles on your all-in
edits.after: Weave Mortal Steel dashes through minions to threaten flank angles on your all-in

edits.before: Save Ultimate for teamfights where the knockup can chain into his team's follow-up
edits.after: Save Fate Sealed for fights where the pull can chain into his team's follow-up

notes: Two kit errors corrected. (1) Soul Unbound (E) was written as a dash in three places; it is not — Yone's spirit leaves his body and is forced back to it, and the existing breakdown.cooldowns line 'punish the body he snaps back to' was the only place that had it right. His actual dash is the empowered Mortal Steel. (2) Fate Sealed was called an 'AoE knockup ultimate'; Riot's text is a blink behind the last champion in a line that PULLS enemies toward him. That matters because knockup-dependent follow-up does not exist off it. Spirit Cleave's 14s shield — the missingInteractions entry for this matchup — was absent from the page entirely and is now in four fields. Chart was split on all seven rows AND the content layer contradicted itself at row 1; both fixed. The packet suspectName 'Your Perfect Execution' is a FALSE POSITIVE. Left alone and worth a look: content.mid says level 6 'flips hard to you' and then that Yone 'claws it back with his own ultimate coming online' — both ults arrive at 6, so the sentence is muddled, but there is no room inside the length band to fix it without rewriting the whole paragraph, and I could not verify which way that specific 4-6 stretch actually resolves. Also unverified: whether Twilight Shroud's untargetability prevents the Soul Unbound spirit from re-applying its stored damage, and whether Fate Sealed's pull can be Flashed after the blink.
